title: Aatmanirbhar Bharat: MoD inks Rs 1,577 crore contracts for Loiter Munition Systems for Indian Army
body_text:
The Ministry of Defence has signed contracts with TATA Advanced Systems Limited and NIBE Private Limited for the procurement of Loiter Munition Systems, along with munitions & other accessories, at an approximate cost of Rs 1,577 crore for the Indian Army. The contracts were inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on August 14, 2026.
The Loiter Munition System is a critical equipment developed to enhance the capability of the Artillery Regiments, thereby strengthening the overall operational effectiveness of the Indian Army. Being procured under the Buy (Indian) category through Fast Track Procedure, the acquisition will bolster the manufacturing capabilities of the Indian industry.
The procurement marks a pivotal step towards modernising and empowering Indian defence industries, which will be a proud flag-bearer of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’.
***
VK/Sa vvy

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed contracts worth approximately Rs 1,577 crore with TATA Advanced Systems Limited and NIBE Private Limited for the procurement of Loiter Munition Systems, along with munitions and accessories, for the Indian Army. The contracts were signed on August 14, 2026 in New Delhi in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. The systems will be procured under the Buy (Indian) category through Fast Track Procedure to strengthen Artillery Regiments' operational capability.
enrichment.context:
Loiter munitions, sometimes called 'kamikaze drones', are precision-guided weapons that can hover over a target area before striking, combining features of drones and missiles. Their induction reflects a global and Indian military shift towards unmanned and networked warfare, accelerated by lessons from recent conflicts such as the Russia-Ukraine and Nagorno-Karabakh wars, where loitering munitions proved decisive in artillery and anti-armour roles.

The procurement categories used by India's defence acquisition system—Buy (Indian), Buy (Indian-IDDM), Buy & Make, etc.—are central to the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' (self-reliant India) push in defence, which aims to reduce import dependence and build domestic manufacturing capacity. The 'Fast Track Procedure' is typically invoked for urgent operational requirements, allowing expedited contracting outside the standard multi-year acquisition timeline. This contract continues a series of recent deals awarded to Indian private defence firms (like TATA Advanced Systems and NIBE) as the government seeks to diversify beyond traditional defence PSUs and build a private domestic defence-industrial base.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Buy (Indian)' category under India's defence procurement procedure primarily refers to which of the following?
options: Procurement of equipment from foreign vendors having an Indian subsidiary
Procurement of equipment from Indian vendors with a minimum indigenous content requirement
Procurement exclusively from Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)
prelims_questions.explanation: The 'Buy (Indian)' category under the Defence Acquisition Procedure mandates procurement from Indian vendors meeting a specified minimum indigenous content, promoting domestic defence manufacturing, as reflected in this contract with TATA Advanced Systems and NIBE Private Limited.

prelims_questions.question: Loiter Munition Systems, as referred to in recent Indian defence procurements, are best described as:
options: Long-range ballistic missiles for strategic deterrence
Precision-guided munitions that can hover over a target area before striking
prelims_questions.explanation: Loiter munitions are unmanned systems that can loiter or hover over a target area, providing surveillance before delivering a precision strike, and are being inducted to strengthen Artillery Regiments.
